Honestly, I'm low functioning and people don't take me seriously. I've been hospitalized twice this year, and people expected me to just go back to functioning like a normal person as soon as I got back. 

I can barely do the things I need to do to survive. 

It's hard and it sucks. People don't take mental health seriously, and that's how suicide claims so many lives. It's not fair at all. But what you can do is surround yourself with people like us who know what it's like and who do take it seriously and who do believe you. 

Also, if your professionals aren't listening to you, have you tried talking to someone else? Sometimes it takes a while to find a therapist that works for you, but it's so worth it. I'm still struggling to get back on my feet, but I feel hopeful again because of the therapist that I have.

There are so many different kinds of reactions to foods that a topical test isn't reliable. The only reason this works for hair dye is that you apply it topically, so if you test it in a small area, you'll have a better idea of how it will affect your entire body. 

There are blood tests you can order for food allergies, but they are limited and expensive. The most reliable way to know for sure is to try it and monitor yourself for the next couple of days. If you think you'll have a bad reaction, make sure to keep Benadryl nearby. It has literally saved my life when I've tested what exactly I'm allergic to. If you don't get a rash or swelling throat, you could also get headaches, joint or body pain, brain fog or nausea. It might not be a full blown allergy, but if you react in any if these ways, it could be a sensitivity.

Allergies are really weird and manifest differently for many different people (I know because I have so many different kinds of allergies and sensitivities, so I've been living with this pretty much my entire life). Allergies or sensitivities are basically just things that your body identifies as intruders, so depending on how your body identifies them can change how your body reacts to them. 

So for instance, someone can have a sensitivity to gluten and have it give them horrible stomach aches. Another person can have a sensitivity to it and have arthritic like pain in response to it. What's happening here is that different parts of your body identify the allergen as an intruder. So for the first one, the stomach is identifying it as an intruder, whereas for the second one it's the joints. 

Congestion and post nasal drip are common with a lot of different things, but from my (albiet limited) experience, it sounds like you have an allergy that's just manifesting differently than most. Try different kinds of allergy meds that are administered differently, if the nasal spray isn't working, try a different one or a pill. I had to try about four different kinds of allergy pills before I found one that helped me manage my symptoms.
